paraphrase: Now the view of the siddhas such as Kapila (the haṭha of mudrās); the difference lies in practice, the fruit is the same. Mahāmudrā, taught by Bhairava: place the left heel at the perineum, stretch out the right leg and hold it firmly with the hands, set the chin on the chest, fill with breath, hold as able and release, on the left then the right side. Placing the stretched leg on the thigh is mahābandha; seated in it one gently strikes the buttocks (the vulgate calls this too mahābandha; it corresponds to mahāvedha).

paraphrase: Layayoga is the dissolution of mind, which arises through 'indications' (saṅketa); Ādinātha — Śiva — taught eight crore of them to his attendants on various mountains. Among them: meditating on the void day and night while standing, walking, sleeping and eating; fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose; meditating on the back of the head; fixing the gaze between the brows; absorption on the big toes; lying on the ground like a corpse, relaxed, in a solitary place. Whoever's mind dissolves by these or other indications — that is layayoga.

paraphrase: Success comes to one who practises; how to one who does not? No success arises from merely reading śāstras. The shaven head, the staff, the ochre robe, reciting 'Nārāyaṇa' or 'namaḥ śivāya', the matted locks and ash, outer worship, worship of the twelve places — how can one without practice, or a cruel person, attain success?
